title: CLAY COUNTY FAIR
full_story:
Last night at the Clay County Fair Maura Kay Smith was crowned JR Miss Clay County Fair.  Maura is the daughter of Dustin and Kathy Smith, Maura is also the Casual Wear and Miss Congeniality.  1st runner up and chosen most photogenic is Karsyn Noll the daughter of Jordan and Amanda Noll, and second runner up and stage presence winner is Kiana Rector the daughter of Ken and Jasmine Rector.  The Peoples Choice award winner was McKynlee Cash the daughter of Dalton and Andrea Cash.  The retiring JR Miss is Halle Patridge.

The Queen contestants pie auction was also held last night, a total of $3,950 was raised, with $850 being the highest bid for a pie.

Today at the Clay County Fair activities start at 8 am with the JR Swine Show followed by the Open Goat Show.  DaS zle Dance and Tumble will perform at 5 pm, admission is free, and the 4H Livestock Auction will begin at 6:30pm.

Look for the WNOI/Clay County Country Swag-N-Wagon for your FREE 99.3FM Clay County Country 10th Anniversary Summer Straw Sun Hat & LeMond Chevrolet Chrysler Black Wayfarer Sunglasses plus kids Sherwin-Williams Sunglasses & Fairfield Save A Lot Patriotic Lollipops for the kids during the 4-H Livestock Auction at The Clay County Agricultural Fair at 6:30pm.

WNOI would like to thank the Clay County Country Club for the use of their golf cart for the WNOI Swag-N-Wagon at the fair.

Tomorrow opens at 8 am with the Open Dairy Show, then at 5 pm Joni’s Power & Grace Tumbling will be in the REA building, admission is free.  The Lickity Split and Legally Sheila concert will be on the stage 7 pm.

The Fair will culminate with the Clay County Fair Queen Pageant Friday night, at 7 pm, with admission $10 for adults and $5 for kids 3 – 10.  There are 13 young ladies vying for the title.  The current Queen is Olivia Haun.

title: JOHNSONVILLE COMMUNITY DAYS
full_story:
Johnsonville Community Days sponsored by the Johnsonville Ruritan Club will start on Friday.  This year’s theme is “Red, White and Rural.”

Friday at 6:30 pm will feature the Truck and Tractor pull, admission is $10 with a $25 hook fee.  There will also be Bingo at 6:30 pm and sandwiches and drinks will be available at the pavilion.

Saturday’s events will include the Flea Market and Craft Fair, 5K, with registration at 6:15 am, and the run walk at 7 am.  The car truck motorcycle and tractor show registration runs from 9 – Noon.  There is a $15 entry fee, for cars, trucks and motorcycles, tractors are free.  There will also be a parade on Saturday with lineup at 9:30 and the parade at 10 am with Harlan Allison as this year’s parade marshal.  At 11, Ham & Beans will be available in the Ruritan building, and a mud bog will start.  At 3:30 the Little Miss and Mister Johnsonville pageant registration will start for those age 3 to 10.  The pageant will begin at 4 pm.  The fish and chicken supper is at 5, and the pedal pull is at 6 pm, and the Kids Power Wheels pull will be at 7 pm.

To enter the car, truck, motorcycle, and tractor show call Lawrence Pennington at 618-919-0297.  To enter the Parade call Ellen Sitze at 618-919-0884 and to enter the mud bog call Kody Payne at 618-383-5883.  To enter the Little Miss and Mister contest call Rachel Johnson at 618-231-1568.

The event wraps up on Sunday with the Community Church service with speaker Travis Mix at 10:30 and the fried chicken meal is at noon.

title: BLOOD DRIVES
full_story:
The American Red Cross announced an emergency blood shortage on July 13th.  Despite thousands of individuals stepping forward to help, the situation has escalated into a blood supply CRISIS.  For just the second time in history, the Red Cross has issued a national blood CRISIS.  Blood donations have fallen to a four-year summer low, worsening this summer’s emergency shortage.  A blood supply crisis is the most extreme blood shortage, posing a concerning risk to patient care.  Doctors will be forced to make difficult decisions about who receives blood transfusions and who will need to wait until more blood products become available.

The American Red Cross needs your help now so that hospital patients can continue to receive the transfusions they need.  All blood types are needed, but the situation is especially dire for type O blood as the Red Cross is now limiting distribution of these blood products to hospitals.  The type O positive blood supply has fallen below a one-day supply.  Blood donors are needed immediately to ensure hospitals have the blood they need for patients whose lives depend on transfusions.

There will be a blood Drive on Friday at the Clay City High School from 1 to 5 pm sponsored by the Clay City High School Student Council.  By donating at this drive, donors are helping one or more graduating seniors earn a scholarship.

The next blood drive in our area will be on Tuesday, August 11th at the Blue Point Free Will Baptist Church from Noon to 6 pm.  Then on Thursday, August 13th there will be a blood drive at the Flora Church of the Nazarene from noon to 5 pm.  People donating at these drives will get a $20 Amazon Gift Card by email.

title: BACK TO SCHOOL VACCINE CLINICS
full_story:
The Clay County Health Department is having a series of Back-to-School vaccine clinics.

The next clinic is on Monday, from 8:30 am to 6 pm at the Health Department on 12th Street.  Appointments are not necessary but are appreciated.  Appointments can be made by calling 618-662-4406.

Illinois state law requires certain immunizations for children and adults enrolled in childcare, school, or college.  State law also mandates immunizations for adults in specific fields of work.

There will also be Clinics on Thursday, August 6th, Wednesday, August 12th, and Thursday, August 13th from 8:30 am to 6 pm.  The final clinic will be from Friday, August 14th from 8 am to Noon.

Again, appointments are not necessary, but appreciated, if you have questions call the Clay County Health Department at 618-662-4406.

title: WILHOUR TRAVELING OFFICE HOURS
full_story:
The next traveling office hours hosted by State Representative Blaine Wilhour will be held on Wednesday, August 5th at the Ramsey Village Hall, from 8:30 to 10:00 am, at the Evans Public Library in Vandalia from 10:30 am to 12:30 pm, and at the Mulberry Grove Village Hall from 2:00 to 3:00 pm.

On Wednesday, August 12th, legislative staff will be available at the Case-Halstead Library in Carlyle from 9:00 to 10:30 am, at the Centralia Regional Library from 11:00 to 12:30 pm, and at the Bryan-Bennett Library in Salem from 2:00 to 3:30 pm.

Then on Wednesday, August 19th legislative staff will be available at the Olney Public Library from 1:00 to 3:00 pm.

Representative Wilhour said “My staff will be available to meet with constituents about public policy issues and concerns as well as provide help with state programs.  I encourage everyone to sign up for my electronic news updates to learn about the activities of the General Assembly and encourage you to take advantage of the online technology to monitor legislative proceedings and file witness slips on legislation that you agree with or disagree with.”

Constituents may contact the district office at 618-665-4109 or online at RepWilhour.com to schedule an appointment to meet with the legislative staff.

title: FALL FISH SALE
full_story:
The Clay County Soil and Water Conservation District is conducting its fall fish sale on Thursday, September 17th at 12:00 pm.

The deadline to order grass carp is Thursday, September 3rd, all other fish orders will be taken by Thursday, September 10th.

Available fish include; Channel Catfish, Largemouth Bass, Hybrid Sunfish, Bluegill, Redear, Fathead Minnows and Grass Carp.

To place your order please contact the Clay County Soil and Water Conservation District at 618 508-8208 ext. 3.
